analysis.title: FOMC – “Medicine starting to work some” as Fed holds rates steady
key_insights: The Fed held rates at 3-3/4 to 4 percent on Oct 28 after a 25bp hike last month. The vote was 12-0-2 in favor of the hold, with two dissents in favor of a hike.
Citi reads Chair Warsh's statements as skewing more dovish than hawkish on the margin. Warsh gave no explicit guidance on upcoming meetings.
Warsh described the tightening of financial conditions as 'medicine starting to work.' He said conditions have tightened but should not be described as tight.
Asked whether policy rates might already be at an appropriate setting, Warsh was noncommittal. That leaves open a hold at the December meeting.

Warsh described growth as accelerating and broadening, and the labor market as robust, resilient and strong. Citi says it does not clearly see the broadening in the data and thinks Warsh overstates the breadth of strength.

Warsh does not see the economy as overheating. He attributes stronger growth to a pickup in productivity and said the Fed should not 'throw sands in the gears' of growth. That implies little urgency to keep hiking.
Warsh said he feels good about the decline in market-based inflation expectations and the stability of consumer inflation expectations. Citi reads this as less urgency to raise rates.
The dissent by Governor Cook in favor of a hike was surprising and marginally dovish according to Citi. Hammack's dissent was expected.
Logan and Kashkari, previous hawkish dissenters, did not dissent. Citi says they presumably assume the committee's base case is a December hike.

In 2027 the Fed will have seven 'live' policy meetings and one strategy meeting instead of eight live meetings. In 2028 it drops to six live meetings and two strategy meetings. Citi guesses the skipped 2027 meeting is October.
Citi's base case is a 25bp hike in December. The risk is another hold if activity data soften, equities fall or credit spreads widen further.
Citi says Warsh will likely have a relatively low bar for a downside surprise. It would not be too surprising if risk-off developments lead to no further hikes this cycle.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The Fed held after a 25bp hike in September. Citi sees the hold as dovish on the margin.
Citi's base case is another hike. Weaker activity data or a further equity selloff with wider credit spreads would make a hold more likely.
Citi says H1 growth was boosted by the bounce back from the government shutdown.
Warsh cited this as growth 'accelerating.' Citi disputes that it is broadening across sectors.

risk_factors: Softer activity data could lead the Fed to hold in December instead of hiking.
Falling equity prices and wider credit spreads could lead the Fed to stop hiking.
Citi says Warsh overstates the breadth of US economic strength, so a downside data surprise could shift the Fed's stance.
vol_and_positioning: Citi's Figure 1 shows market pricing before and after the Fed statement, but the text gives no levels.

tension_points.bull_case: Citi's base case is a 25bp hike in December. Warsh says growth is strong and accelerating, and the committee's base case involves a December hike per Logan and Kashkari's assent.
tension_points.bear_case: Warsh does not see overheating, believes productivity lifts growth without inflation, and is pleased with falling inflation expectations. He was noncommittal on whether rates are already appropriate.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Softer activity data, or falling equity prices and wider credit spreads, would make another hold more likely.

theme_stances.key_argument: Warsh's comments suggest little urgency to raise policy rates further, so the risk is another hold if activity softens or financial conditions tighten.

theme_stances.key_argument: Warsh said tighter financial conditions are the medicine starting to work and productivity growth means strong growth will not be inflationary.
